detector:
**Under-charted strumming detector: results against the six human charts, and the test-song flags**

## Verdict

The detector is not good enough to drive a chart change.

- **Target case.** In windows where SPL-A has fewer than half the onsets the detected rate implies, the human chart has at least N/2 more onsets only 27% of the time (6/22). Under leave-one-song-out it is 22% (6/27). Flagging every window where our chart has fewer than 1 onset per beat, with no audio at all, does as well: 26% (10/39), with higher recall.
- **The human rarely charts the detected rate.** In flagged windows the human chart writes the detected 8ths or 16ths 4–5% of the time.
- **The test-song case is almost absent from the six songs.** Only 6 of 269 windows are clearly under-charted (human at least 2× ours and at least N more onsets). Every true hit comes from two passages: the Take Me Out intro and Kimochi Warui 167–176 s.
- **16th detection does not work:** 0 of 22 right on the five songs.
- **The bleed controls barely matter.** No sign that hi-hats drive the guitar-stem pulse where the guitar is active. The friend's 2:32–2:35 window is drumless, so bleed cannot explain it there.
- **Use it at most as a "listen here" list.**

## Detector definition

**Signal**
- 6s guitar and drum stems, mono, at 44.1 kHz. STFT with a Hann window, n_fft 1024, hop 128, keeping only the 2–7 kHz bins.
- Band energies per frame:
  - E_G = Σ|G|² (guitar stem).
  - E_D = Σ|D|² (drum stem).
  - E_R = Σ|G|²·[|G|² > |D|²]: only the cells where the guitar stem is louder than the drum stem. This is the hi-hat control (the "dominance" control). It was chosen before the evaluation: hi-hat bleed is weaker in the guitar stem than in the drum stem, and the control does not remove guitar strums that coincide with hats.
- Envelope in dB: L = 10·log10(E + 1e-6·P95(E_G)).

**Windows**
- Two measures of the built chart's grid, non-overlapping. Every chart here is 4/4 from tick 0 (checked), so N = 8 beats.
- One-measure windows were also computed and are reported.
- Why two measures was chosen before the evaluation:
  - twice the 8th cycles at the same false-alarm rate;
  - only N = 8 has bins that a 1-bar pattern cannot fill, which the null below needs;
  - a chart fix would act on phrases, not single bars.

**Modulation ratios**
- L is sampled at 48 points per beat between the window's beats, linearly detrended, and taken through a rectangular-window DFT, giving the power P(k) with k/N cycles per beat.
- ref = median P(k) over the bins whose frequency, (k/N) divided by the mean beat period, lies in 3–25 Hz, leaving out whole cycles-per-beat bins.
- r_q = P(qN)/ref: q = 2 is the 8th rate, q = 4 the 16th rate, q = 1 the quarter rate.

**Rule**
- Active: the window's mean E_R is at least P95(E_G) − 30 dB.
- 16ths: active, r4 ≥ T and r4 > r2.
- 8ths: otherwise, active and r2 ≥ T.
- Flag "under-charted": our onsets < 0.5 × q × N, with q = 2 or 4 onsets per beat.

**Threshold**
- T = 20, fixed a priori: the 99th percentile of the statistic's empirical null.
- The null is the odd bins (periodicities only a 2-bar pattern can make), 13,484 bins over all seven songs, measured without the human charts: p50 0.78, p99 20.3, p99.9 49.8, P(>10) 0.034.
- T = 10 (the brief's threshold) and a leave-one-song-out search are also reported.

**Other controls computed**
- The same ratios on the drum stem.
- rho: the guitar band envelope's correlation with the drum stem's, per window.
- Q: an envelope-level regression of E_G on E_D at lags −2..+2 frames, skipped when the drum band is at least 40 dB below the guitar's P95.

**Rejected or changed after the first runs, on grounds not taken from the human charts**
- **Complex coherent regression (rejected).** It removed 30–58% of the guitar band energy in the test song's drumless 148.8–165.7 s. The near-silent drum stem holds a faint copy of the guitar.
- **Q's 40 dB gate (added).** Without it, Q fitted coefficients up to 1e7 on drumless windows and erased guitar pulses.
- **Also added later:** an 8ths-only rule (V3) and attack-salience features.

## Ground truth (human Expert guitar, against our grid)

- n_h and n_o: human and our onsets in [start − 30 ms, end − 30 ms).
- Human writes 8ths: at least 75% of the window's 8th slots hold a human onset within min(70 ms, beat/8). Human writes 16ths: the same on the 16th slots.
- Precision counts, for flagged windows:
  - P1: n_h > n_o;
  - P2: n_h ≥ n_o + N/2;
  - P3: the human charts the detected rate.
- Recall denominators:
  - U1: n_h > n_o;
  - U2: n_h ≥ n_o + N/2;
  - U3: clearly under, n_h ≥ 2·n_o and n_h ≥ n_o + N.

## Held-out results (leave one song out)

Each fold chooses the guitar envelope (no control, dominance, regression, or both), the rule (V1, V2, V3) and T on five songs, then is scored on the sixth. Only held-out numbers are given here.

**Target objective (F1 of the flag against U2):**
- Five songs: 27 flags. P1 0.48 (13/27), P2 0.22 (6/27), P3 0.04. Recall of U1 0.12, U2 0.15 (6/41), U3 1/6.
- Per song, with the fold's choice:

|---|---|---|---|---|
| TMO | R/V2/5 | 11 | 4/11 | 4/9 |
| ATST | Q/V2/30 | 0 | – | – |
| Creep | Q/V2/30 | 2 | 0/2 | 0/12 |
| KW | R/V1/5 | 5 | 2/5 | 2/7 |
| DD | R/V1/5 | 9 | 0/9 | 0/12 |
| Lucretia | Q/V2/30 | 0 | – | 0/21 |

- The choices are unstable across folds. Over the whole grid the objective is flat (0.11–0.17).

**Agreement objective (8ths against human 8ths):**
- Five songs: P 0.67 (147/218), R 0.82. That is no better than always answering "8ths".
- Lucretia: P 0.87, R 0.98, against a base rate of 0.88.
- 16ths: P 0.14 (6/43) on the five songs.

**One-measure windows:**
- A priori: 28 flags, P1 0.54, P2 0.36, P3 0.18, recall of U2 0.11.
- Held out (target objective): 57 flags, P2 0.25, recall of U2 0.16.

**Within windows that are both sparse (ours < N) and active:**
- 2 measures, a priori rule: flagged windows hold U2 3/11 times, unflagged 1/16 (Fisher p 0.17).
- The post-hoc 8ths-only rule gives 3/6 against 1/21. All hits are the two passages named in the verdict, and the windows are not independent.

**Feature AUC against human 8ths:**
- The 8th-rate ratio r2: 0.69–0.81 on five songs, 0.40 on Kimochi Warui.
- Our chart's own onsets per beat: 0.62–0.99. So the existing chart already predicts human 8ths better than the audio feature does.

**Bleed:**
- In active windows with drums, rho medians are −0.10 to 0.14.
- Cells where the drum stem is louder hold a median of 0–5% of the guitar band energy (p90 at most 0.20, highest on All the Small Things).
- Windows with a guitar 8th pulse ≥ 20, a drum 8th pulse ≥ 20 and rho ≥ 0.5: 0–3 per song, 1 in the test song.
- In drumless windows rho is high (test song median 0.72) because of the guitar copy in the drum stem. So rho is not a bleed signal on its own.

## Not measured

- **What the guitar actually plays.** There are no isolated stems or tabs. "The human writes 8ths" is a charting decision used as a proxy.
- **The test song itself.** It has no human chart, so no flag is verified. The only evidence is the friend's report for 2:32–2:35.
- **The target case.** It rests on 3–6 hits from two passages. The windows are not independent and no confidence intervals were computed; with counts this small they would be very wide.
- **Bleed.** There is no ground truth for it; the controls were judged only by internal consistency.
- **Lucretia's truth is unreliable.** Only 27% of our beats fall within 70 ms of a human beat, so the slot occupancy there is not trustworthy. It is reported separately.
- **Also untested:** swing and triplet feel, the ft stems, and other takes. No chart change was made or scored, and there was no playtest.
- **The brief's own numbers.** `rhythm_227.py` and `phase_227.py` do not compute the 2–7 kHz measure. `repro_brief.py` reproduces it at 18× and 26× (dB envelope, Hann window), against the brief's 17× and 21×, with 15 flagged 4-s windows against about 16. The value depends strongly on the envelope variant: 148–152 s gives 18–40×, 164–168 s gives 4–26×.

**What I checked:** the report's headline numbers match its own outputs (`tables_out.txt` lines 14, 131, 134–157; `diag_out.txt` sections 1–5). I did not re-run the feature extraction or the evaluation. The confidence intervals below are ones I added (95% Wilson); the report did not compute any.

## What failed

The fill would add strums at the detected rate in every flagged window, so it needs two things to be true. First, flagged windows must really be under-charted. Second, the human must chart the detected rate there. The six songs show neither.

1. **Flags are mostly wrong when tested on unseen songs.** Leave-one-song-out, five songs: the human has at least N/2 more onsets than us in 6 of 27 flagged windows (0.22, CI 0.11–0.41). The a priori detector gets 6/22 (0.27, CI 0.13–0.48). So about three in four filled windows would add notes the human did not write.
2. **The audio adds nothing over a rule that ignores audio.** Flagging every window where our chart has fewer than 1 onset per beat gives 10/39 (0.26, CI 0.15–0.41), with higher recall: 10/41 under-charted windows found, against 6/41.
3. **The human rarely charts the rate the fill would add.** In flagged windows the human writes the detected 8ths or 16ths in 1 of 27 held-out (0.04, CI 0.01–0.18) and 1 of 22 a priori. Even in a correct window, a full 8th grid would mostly overshoot.
4. **16th detection fails:** 0 of 22 right, a priori.
5. **The audio feature is weak and unstable.** r2 (the 8th-rate pulse) separates human-8ths windows at AUC 0.69–0.81 on five songs but 0.40 on Kimochi Warui (worse than chance). Our chart's own density does better: 0.62–0.99.
6. **The parameter choices are not stable across folds.** The best target score over the whole grid is 0.11–0.17, and folds pick different envelopes, rules and thresholds (T from 5 to 30). Leave-one-song-out tuning of a fill would be choosing noise.
7. **The case we want to fix barely occurs in the six songs.** Only 6 of 269 windows are clearly under-charted (human at least 2× ours and at least N more onsets). The detector finds 1 of those 6 a priori and in the held-out run. All true hits come from two passages: the Take Me Out intro and Kimochi Warui 167–176 s.
8. **The only promising lead was found after looking at the results.** The 8ths-only rule (V3), within sparse active windows, gives 3/6 against 1/21 (Fisher p 0.025, CI 0.19–0.81). It was devised after the first runs, its three hits are those same two passages, and the windows are not independent.
9. **The friend's window isn't flagged anyway.** For 148.8–152.2 s input (2:32.1–2:35.5 song time), r2 is 17, below the a priori T = 20. It is flagged only at T = 10. At that threshold the a priori 2-bar null's false-alarm rate per bin is 0.034 (3.4%), against 1.0% at T = 20.

## What evidence would be needed

- **Ground truth for what the guitar plays,** not how a human charted it. Isolated guitar multitracks or verified tabs for some songs would let us score the pulse directly and separate a missed strum from a charting choice.
- **Many more examples of the target case, on songs never used to set thresholds.** With 6 clear cases, precision can't be pinned within ±0.2. About 100 flags gives roughly ±0.1. At about 4–5 flags per song that is around 20–25 more songs with human Expert guitar charts. They should lean towards strummed rhythm parts (pop-punk, indie, alt-rock), since that is where the case occurs.
- **A pass bar set before testing**, for example:
  - held-out "at least N/2 more onsets" precision of at least 0.5, with its lower 95% bound above the no-audio rule (about 0.26);
  - "human charts the detected rate" precision of at least 0.5;
  - doing better than the chart's own density, not only better than chance.
- **The 8ths-only rule (V3) tested with its threshold fixed beforehand.** It is the only lead, and a fresh song set would show whether 3/6 holds.
- **A check of the test-song flags by ear.** Someone (the friend or another charter) marks which of the 8 flagged stretches at T = 20, plus the 9 added at T = 10, really have audible 8th strums. This is the only way to verify anything on the test song, and it would also show whether T = 10 is right there.
- **Once a detector passes:** the paired SPL-A vs SPL-A+fill score (F1@50, F1@100, precision, recall, density ratio, lane measures) on all songs, with no song getting worse beyond a tolerance set in advance, and then a playtest.

Averaged around drum-band attacks, the dominance envelope R falls 4-11 dB: test 87.9 s from -0.2 to -4.8 dB, test 121.7 s from -2.6 to -6.5, ATST 45.2 s from +0.3 to -10.6, ATST 90.9 s from +1.9 to -7.9, KW 162.7 s from -3.5 to -10.7.

- **Test song, T = 20:** in 121.7-125.1 s (2:05.1-2:08.4) the control raises r2 from 14.8 to 55.7. A variant that caps those cells at the bin's window median instead of zeroing them gives 18.6. So this flag is made by the control and does not show a guitar pulse. It also raises r2 from 14.6 to 32.0 at 108.2 s (capped variant: 23.3).
- **Test song, T = 10:** 67.6-71.0 s (G2 3.8 to R2 11.1; capped 6.8) and 115.0-118.3 s (9.2 to 18.6) are flagged only with the control. The report's T = 10 table does not say so.
- **All the Small Things:** all 3 flags are anti-phase and all are wrong (human 0, 0 and 8 onsets).
- The report's "no sign that hi-hats drive the guitar-stem pulse" is therefore not supported.
- Phase does not separate hits from misses (4 of the 6 hits are in anti-phase windows), so this does not show that the hits are artefacts.

flaws.issue:
T = 20 is presented as the 99th percentile of the statistic's null, and the FILL report calls 3.4% / 1.0% the false-alarm rate. But that null comes from odd bins, which only a 2-bar pattern can fill. The tested 8th bin repeats every bar, and any beat-locked pattern fills such bins:
- The untested even (1-bar) bins exceed 20 in 2.6% of cases (p99 35.6), against 1.0% for the odd bins.
- In active windows where the human writes at most 2 onsets in 8 beats, R2 >= 20 in 4/14 (0.29).
- Where the human fills fewer than 25% of the 8th slots, R2 >= 20 in 5/19 (0.26).
flaws.effect: The practical false-alarm rate at T = 20 is about 25-30%, not 1%, so T = 20 is not an a priori 1% test. The verdict is unchanged.

flaws.issue: The detector report gives the 1-measure held-out result (target objective) as 57 flags, P2 0.25, U2 recall 0.16. Its own tables_out.txt (line 328) and my independent LOSO re-run both give 59 flags, P2 13/59 = 0.22, recall 13/90 = 0.14.
flaws.effect: A small numeric error, in the optimistic direction. The verdict is unchanged.

flaws.issue:
Both reports, and the brief, treat the friend's window (148.8-152.2 s input) as an 8th-rate case just under the threshold. The same beat-locked statistic says otherwise:
- In that window the beat-rate ratio r1 is 59 and r2 only 17. r2 = 17 is below the test song's median r2 over active windows (26.8).
- The four drumless 2-bar windows after it (152.2-165.7 s) have r1 53-68 and r2 1.7-10.
- The beat-folded envelope in 148.8-152.2 swings about 4 dB once per beat and does not rise on the off-beat 8th. Attacks are soft: there is no 6-dB flux peak in 148.8-155.5.
- Under the report's own rule V2 (r2 >= r1) these windows are never flagged at any T.
- Our chart has 2-5 onsets per 8 beats across 148.8-165.7.
- If 'original-song 2:32-2:35' means the recording's own clock (input 152-155 s), that window has r2 = 1.7.
flaws.effect:
Lowering T, or adding an 8th fill, would not address the friend's passage. If it is under-charted, it is at the beat rate. Neither report tested that.

An exploratory quarter-rate rule, chosen after the fact, gets 6 flags and 1 hit on the five songs. But the references hold only 11 active 2-bar windows where we have fewer than 0.5 onsets per beat, so they cannot test it. The 'no fill' conclusion is unaffected.

flaws.issue: The test-song flags depend on an untested analysis choice. A Hann taper on the beat-locked DFT barely moves the reference results (five songs: 21 flags, P2 7/21, U2 recall 7/41).
flaws.effect:
On the test song the Hann taper changes the flags:
- 2-bar, T = 20: 3 of the 10 flagged windows drop (30.5, 206.2 and 368.5 s) and 74.4 s appears.
- 1-bar, T = 10: 10 of the 27 drop and 8 new ones appear.
- The friend's window gets 12.4.

The 'listen here' list is unstable and should carry that caveat.

flaws.issue:
Wording:
- **'Over the whole grid the objective is flat (0.11-0.17)':** 0.11 is the grid median and 0.17 the best (diag section 5), not the range.
- **The FILL report's 'with 6 clear cases, precision can't be pinned within ±0.2':** precision is over the 22-27 flags (Wilson ±0.15-0.18); 6 is a recall denominator.
- **'five songs' in the AUC line:** it means every song except Kimochi Warui, Lucretia included, unlike everywhere else.
flaws.effect: None of these changes a result.

verify.corrected_conclusion:
The detector's numbers reproduce exactly on all seven songs, and the verdict holds: the detector is not good enough to drive a chart change. The fill was rightly not built, and there is nothing to re-score.

Corrections:
1. **The hits.** 3 of the 6 hits (P2: human at least ours + N/2), a priori and held out, are 16th flags in the body of Take Me Out, not in the two passages the reports name. Counting 8th-rate flags only: 3 of 9 are hits, and 1 of 9 is where the human writes 8ths.
2. **The hi-hat control is not neutral.** It cuts notches at hi-hat hits. It created the test-song flag at 2:05.1-2:08.4 (and 67.6-71.0 s at T = 10). 12 of the 22 reference flags have guitar and drum pulses in opposite phase. So "no sign that hi-hats drive the pulse" is not supported.
3. **The false-alarm rate.** At T = 20 it is about 0.26-0.29 in active windows where the human charts almost nothing, not the 1% the odd-bin null suggests.
4. **The 1-measure held-out result** is 59 flags, P2 0.22, recall 0.14, not 57, 0.25 and 0.16.
5. **The test-song flags change with a Hann taper** (3 of 10 drop at T = 20). Treat the list as tentative.
6. **The friend's 2:32-2:35.** The guitar band there, and in the drumless 152-166 s input after it, pulses mainly once per beat (r1 53-68, r2 2-17). Our chart has 2-5 onsets per 8 beats, below quarter-note density. An 8th fill, or a lower T, is not the remedy, and neither report tested under-charting at the beat rate. The six references cannot test it (only 11 such sparse active windows).

Not measured: whether the friend meant too few notes or notes out of sync; what the guitar actually plays there. Checking it by ear remains the only way to verify.
